clue.text: A political leader was complimentary and that's valued

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the leading letter of the word political
to have praised someone is to have been complimentary

explanation.surface: A party chief spoke well of something, and that shows it was prized.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Political leader' is the first letter of political, P, not a party head.
explanation.definitionFit: Something appraised has been assessed for worth, i.e. valued, a straightforward synonym.

indicators.note: in a down entry, standing up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a bluff is a pretence, a pose

explanation.surface: A frank, honest teller of moral tales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bluff' looks like an adjective (frank) but is a noun, a pretence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek fabulist wrote fables each ending with a moral, so he is a moralist.

definitions.meaning: in vain means futile, without purpose
something blunt lacks a sharp tip

explanation.surface: Frankly, it was utterly futile.
explanation.definitionFit: It means futile, and literally lacking a point, like a blunt blade.

clue.text: Quite mouthwatering — but gets a pip in by accident

indicators.note: the letters fall together haphazardly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tasty fruit dish, though a seed slipped in by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetising food stimulates the appetite, making the mouth water.

clue.text: He wrote of war and special forces with dispatch

parts.note: the SAS is the British Army's Special Air Service
dispatch means speed, so with dispatch means promptly or soon

explanation.surface: A war writer describes elite troops sent out on missions.
explanation.walkthrough: Siegfried Sassoon was a First World War poet; 'dispatch' suggests sending, but here means speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Siegfried Sassoon was a First World War poet who wrote about life in the trenches.

clue.text: Dispute as daughter is told to go

parts.note: taken as written
someone sent away has been told to go

explanation.surface: A family row as the daughter is ordered out.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissent is disagreement, a dispute with an accepted view.

clue.text: Left to fill in, gave voice in inappropriate language

indicators.note: one letter is set to fill the inside of another word, so it goes within it

parts.note: to give voice can mean to sing, past tense sang

explanation.surface: Someone stepped in as a stand-in singer and used rude words.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is informal speech, unsuitable for formal settings, so inappropriate language describes it.

parts.note: a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A youngster makes a quick mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A skid is a slide out of control, a literal slip.

definitions.meaning: to tolerate or put up with

explanation.surface: A real living bear.
explanation.definitionFit: It means both to dwell somewhere and to tolerate something.

clue.text: Deny a gem's being reset for the waiting youth

indicators.note: a gem being reset is placed in a new setting, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A jewel is refused for a young server.
explanation.walkthrough: Ganymede, in Greek myth, was the youth who served as cupbearer to the gods; his name is used for young waiters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganymede was the cupbearer of the gods, so young male servers are called by his name.

indicators.note: the letter for many is put in the word for spring

parts.note: to skip is to spring or hop
M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, stands for many

explanation.surface: Come springtime, lots of people tighten their belts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season but is the verb, a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp is to economise by spending or using less than one should.

definitions.meaning: a ... can be a slight trace or hint, as in a ... of garlic
doubt about whether something is believable is a ... of it

explanation.surface: A clue suggests that someone is not quite believable.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a faint trace (a hint) and mistrust (a gap in belief).

clue.text: One who's asked to peer in it may well get upset

indicators.note: to upset something is to knock it over, so these letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone invited to look into a well might be overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May well' is linking padding; 'get upset' tells you to rearrange TO PEER IN IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A petitioner is someone who has made a formal request, one who has asked for something.

clue.text: A word used among master mariners

indicators.note: the letters sit among the words master mariners, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: A piece of jargon common among sea captains.
explanation.definitionFit: A term is a word or expression, especially a technical one.

parts.note: reads as running at present, but currently also means by electric current

explanation.surface: Describing something now working.
explanation.definitionFit: A device with its power flowing is running by electric current.

indicators.note: bad here means badly arranged, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Betrayal, though the people concerned are not so wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is betrayal of one's country, the gravest form of double-dealing or treachery.

indicators.note: the letters play about and so rearrange

explanation.surface: Identify a craftsman who plays darts.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman is a skilled manual worker, a synonym of artisan.

clue.text: Reached high to marry, taking in royalty

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word for royalty is taken into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: to wed is to marry
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen and so for royalty

explanation.surface: A social climber aimed high by marrying into the royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: To have towered is to have risen to a great height, reaching high above others.

clue.text: Look again at cutback in army personnel and secret weapon

indicators.note: the cut word goes in between the other pieces

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are British army personnel
a mine is a concealed explosive weapon
read as two words: axe (to fell or slash) and back, which turns that word round

explanation.surface: Reviewing cuts in the army and a hidden weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutback' looks like a reduction but splits into a synonym of axe and back, giving EXA.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect something a second time is to look at it again.

parts.note: alludes to the proverb that being away makes the heart grow fonder

explanation.surface: Asking what makes a bond grow stronger.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says being away from someone increases fondness, so being gone strengthens love.

clue.text: They'll eliminate faltering fool without hesitation

parts.note: a faltering speaker says er

indicators.note: means outside, so the fool goes around the hesitation

parts.note: an ass is a fool
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: They'll get rid of a stumbling idiot who speaks smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside, not lacking; 'faltering' supplies a stammered extra sound at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasers remove marks, so they eliminate pencil writing.

parts.note: reads as tree boughs above, but means branched horns growing on a deer's head

explanation.surface: Looking up at the boughs of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag's horns are branched and grow on top of its head, branches over the head.

parts.note: reads as collapsing, but means splitting something into its components for study

explanation.definitionFit: To analyse is to separate something into its parts, breaking it down.

parts.note: a scout sent to gather information is a spy

explanation.surface: Picking out an English reconnaissance soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, i.e. to spot something.

clue.text: Article included in wages in the Philippines

indicators.note: the article is included in the word for wages

parts.note: pay is wages
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An item in the pay packet in the Philippines.
explanation.definitionFit: Panay is one of the major islands of the Philippines, found there.

clue.text: To put it another way, the letters appear rash

indicators.note: it is the letters of appear rash, not the words, that make the answer when reordered

explanation.surface: Restating something, the writing looks hasty.
explanation.definitionFit: To paraphrase is to express a statement in different words, putting it another way.

clue.text: A woman, going to extremes, gets flat

parts.note: Eve, the first woman, is a common girl's name
the north and south poles are the extremes, N and S

explanation.surface: A woman goes too far and ends up in a flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' suggests a home; here it is level.
explanation.definitionFit: To even something is to make it level, the same as making it flat.

indicators.note: the piece is given more than once, here twice

parts.note: one is I, so one's (one is) gives I plus S

explanation.surface: Someone keeps running water.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isis is the name of the River Thames as it flows through Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isis is the stretch of the River Thames at Oxford, a flowing river.

parts.note: reads as men alone backing down, but describes a secluded house reserved for male religious

explanation.surface: Only the men are falling back in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A house for monks is a retreat from the world where only men live.

parts.note: the head of the word dunder is its first letter
to rive is an old word meaning to split or tear apart

explanation.surface: Force the idiot to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dunderhead' looks like an idiot but is read as dunder's head, its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive someone to do something is to force or compel them.

parts.note: dithering means saying one thing
then saying the opposite

explanation.surface: Asking whether a certain poet was indecisive.
explanation.walkthrough: Alfred Noyes was an English poet, author of The Highwayman.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Noyes was an English poet and author of The Highwayman.

parts.note: reads as an exacting standard of goods, but describes a strict, exacting character trait

explanation.surface: Insisting on high standards.
explanation.definitionFit: Severity or strictness of manner is a demanding trait of character.
